payload.question_text: Which factor can lower speech recognition accuracy?

options.error_type: Confuses audio conditions with language modeling
options.rationale: Vocabulary helps predict likely word sequences after speech sounds are analyzed. It does not describe an audio condition that makes the microphone capture less clear.
options.better_fit: Use this when improving likely word choices, especially for specialized terms.

feedback.intrinsic: The call may still be hard to transcribe because the loud sound remains in the recording.
feedback.instructional: Start with the audio conditions: background noise directly affects recognition accuracy.

options.rationale: Background noise can make captured speech less clear. It can confuse recognition and lower accuracy.
Low delay makes a live interaction feel responsive. It does not make noisy audio clearer.
options.better_fit: Use this when planning how quickly a live response must arrive.

feedback.intrinsic: People may receive a fast transcript that is still inaccurate in a noisy area.
feedback.instructional: Latency is response delay; noise is an audio-quality concern.

options.error_type: Confuses audio input with text post-processing
options.rationale: Punctuation restoration improves readability after words are transcribed. It does not improve the quality of the captured speech.
options.better_fit: Use this when making a completed transcript easier to read.

feedback.intrinsic: The transcript may look neater while words affected by noise remain wrong.
feedback.instructional: Punctuation is added after recognition; background noise affects the earlier audio capture.

payload.explanation: Correct. Background noise can make spoken words harder to recognize.

payload.question_text: What should a team verify for language and dialect support? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Support must include the languages users need. Language requirements differ across languages.

options.error_type: Confuses language support with audio quality
options.rationale: Microphone distance affects captured audio quality. It does not determine which languages or dialects are supported.
options.better_fit: Use this when assessing audio capture conditions for recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: A suitable microphone position would not add support for a needed regional variation.
feedback.instructional: Language support concerns what people speak; microphone distance concerns how clearly speech is captured.

options.rationale: Regional variations are dialects. A team should verify that required dialects are supported.
For spoken input, the capability must understand the required languages and variations. Support should be checked before implementation.

payload.explanation: Correct. Verify the target languages, regional variations, and the ability to handle them.

payload.question_text: Microphone quality affects only speech synthesis, not speech recognition accuracy.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team could focus on spoken output while poor recordings continue to cause inaccurate transcripts.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Microphone quality is part of audio capture for recognition. It affects how clearly spoken words are recorded.

payload.explanation: Correct. Microphone quality affects the audio captured for recognition, so it can affect accuracy.

payload.question_text: Teams should verify target language and regional dialect support before implementation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A launch could leave some intended users unable to use voice features as expected.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Verify required languages and dialects before implementation so the capability matches the people it serves.

payload.explanation: Correct. Speech sounds and requirements differ across languages and regional variations.

payload.question_text: Which approach fits an application that needs to understand spoken commands?

options.error_type: Confuses spoken input with spoken output
options.rationale: Speech synthesis converts written text into spoken audio. It does not turn a spoken command into text.
options.better_fit: Use this when text must be spoken aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The application could speak a reply but would not capture what the person said.
feedback.instructional: Use recognition for spoken input and synthesis for spoken output.

options.error_type: Confuses solution selection with a synthesis stage
options.rationale: Text normalization prepares written text for pronunciation in speech synthesis. It is not the capability for understanding spoken commands.
options.better_fit: Use this when preparing written text for pronunciation.

feedback.intrinsic: The application may prepare outgoing text well while the spoken command remains unrecognized.
feedback.instructional: Text normalization is one synthesis stage; speech recognition handles incoming spoken words.

options.rationale: Speech recognition converts spoken words into written text. It fits an application that must understand spoken commands.

options.error_type: Confuses solution selection with a recognition stage
options.rationale: Beam search is a decoding technique that selects a likely transcription. It is not the overall capability selected for spoken input.
options.better_fit: Use this when selecting the best transcription during recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing this stage alone would not describe the full approach needed for voice commands.
feedback.instructional: Select speech recognition for the capability; beam search is one part of its decoding process.

payload.explanation: Correct. Speech recognition converts spoken input into text so commands can be understood.

payload.question_text: Which statements describe latency? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Latency means delay. In speech work, it describes waiting time.

options.text: It occurs between input and output
options.rationale: Latency is measured from user input to output. This describes the timing relationship.
Microphone quality concerns how clearly audio is captured. Latency concerns how long processing takes.
options.better_fit: Use this when evaluating how clearly audio is captured.

feedback.intrinsic: A team could measure delay carefully while poor microphone capture still harms recognition.
feedback.instructional: Separate timing from audio quality: latency is input-to-output delay.

options.rationale: Live conversations need low latency to feel responsive. Long waits create friction.

payload.explanation: Correct. Latency is the delay from user input to output and is especially important in live conversations.

payload.question_text: Speech synthesis is the right capability when an application must convert spoken commands into text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A person could speak a command, but the application would not have the text needed to understand it.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Match recognition to spoken input. Match speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech, to spoken output.

payload.explanation: Correct. Speech recognition converts spoken commands into text; synthesis creates spoken audio from text.

payload.question_text: Which planning area covers how audio is stored and protected?

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with audio conditions
options.rationale: Audio quality concerns noise, microphones, distance, and bandwidth. It does not cover storage or protection of audio data.
options.better_fit: Use this when assessing noise or microphone quality.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording may be clear while its handling still fails to protect sensitive information.
feedback.instructional: Choose privacy and compliance for questions about processing, storage, and protection.

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with language support
options.rationale: Language support concerns target languages and regional speech variations. It does not describe how audio data is protected.
options.better_fit: Use this when checking supported speech variations.

feedback.intrinsic: Supporting a caller's dialect would not answer how their audio is stored safely.
feedback.instructional: Keep language support separate from privacy obligations.

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with processing delay
options.rationale: Latency is the delay between input and output. It does not address data storage or protection.
options.better_fit: Use this when setting response-time needs.

feedback.intrinsic: Fast responses would not protect audio that is handled improperly.
feedback.instructional: Latency concerns timing; privacy and compliance concern responsible audio-data handling.

options.rationale: Privacy and compliance cover how audio is processed, stored, protected, and regulated. This is the planning area for data handling.

payload.explanation: Correct. Privacy and compliance address how audio data is handled and protected.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Long pauses can make a live exchange feel slow and interrupt the flow of conversation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Real-time conversations need low latency, while batch transcription can tolerate more delay.

payload.explanation: Correct. Low latency helps a live conversation feel responsive.

payload.question_text: Privacy and compliance only matter when audio is processed, not when it is stored.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Sensitive audio could be stored without the needed safeguards even if its processing was considered.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Privacy and compliance cover processing, storage, protection, and regulatory requirements for audio data.

payload.explanation: Correct. Audio storage is also part of privacy and compliance planning.

metadata.unit_slo: Assess the main requirements before adding speech to an application.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.
